title: Swap out the bespoke logging console and use the macOS Console app as the menubar app's log viewer, as Utilz menuz does
body:
Swap out the bespoke logging console functionality and use the macOS Console app as the visual log viewer for the menubar app. See how this is done in the Utilz menuz menubar app (hv, 17 Oct 2026: "one thing that menuz does that I really like that would simplify Intent, Conflab and Gtools").

How menuz does it (Utilz, `native/macos/Menuz`): every run appends to one log file, `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/menuz/menuz.log`, and the menu's `Open Log` item opens that file with `/usr/bin/open` (`MenuzApp.openLog`, a failure logged and never dropped), which hands a `.log` file to the macOS Console app: search, filtering, live follow and a window are Console's, not the app's. `utilz menuz log` tails the same file in a terminal, and the app's own messages go to OSLog (`Logger`), which Console also shows. There is no console window controller, no tailing view, no log model and no log buffer in the app.

The change here: drop the app's own console window and the code that tails and renders the log behind it, and put one item in the menu that opens the log file (or the daemon's log file) in Console. Keep the CLI's `log`/tail verb for the terminal. Measure what the current console shows that a plain log file would not (eg a daemon's log that is not a file, or coloured levels) before removing it, and route that into the file or OSLog first.

## Scope widened by hv, 2026-10-22

hv, first-hand in ic's session on 2026-10-22, after ic proposed an `Open Logs` item, a busy line and a warning line of the app's own: "PLEASE. PLEASE. PLEASE. PLEASE. Look at how Menuz and Gtools do the masthead row of their menubar apps. I DO NOT WANT A NEW BESPOKE INCOMPATIBLE VERSION. I want them all to use the same controls the same way so that they look the same. Don't make repeat myself. Again. Again."

So the menu takes the controls Gtools and Menuz already have, copied rather than designed:

- arca_swift's `MastheadRow` on top, as Gtools has it: `IntentMasthead` for the values the app owns, `MastheadPlacement` keeping the row at the top of the newest menu, and the `Masthead/` resources (`masthead.yaml`, `about.md`, `about.css` and the logo). It replaces the app's own bold identity row.
- Gtools' layout A (gtools#0108), with the intentd row, its name over its state as the row's second line, and its flyout, `intentd > Open | Start | Stop | Restart`, in place of the flat Start, Stop and Restart items. A verb in flight shows as the caption that stands in for it.
- menuz's `Log` item in place of the Console: `Log`, or `Log (no log yet)` and disabled until a log exists, opening the logs in the macOS Console app.

Open question for hv: arca_swift 0.1.1 declares `.macOS(.v26)` and swift-tools 6.2, so adopting it raises Intent.app's floor from macOS 14 to 26, as Gtools and Menuz have it.

Ruled by vc under hv's pen, 2026-10-22: contract L5 asks only about criteria still in scope, so ST0075's seven test rows over its withdrawn Console criteria can be re-kinded non-test and set n/a; the guard lands first, as its own bank, `refs/bank/ic/0607/l5`.
